Sieve's target users are tutors teaching local Singapore students,
whose phone numbers are 8 digits. AB3 accepted any run of 3 or more
digits.

Let's strip all non-digit characters before validating, so formatted input
such as "9123 4567" or "(9123)-4567" is accepted and stored as
"91234567".

Storing only digits lets duplicate detection compare phones reliably.

Strip in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a data file with a
hand-edited, formatted phone still loads instead of being discarded.
The Phone constructor stays strict and accepts only 8 digits.

Require 8-digit phone numbers

Sieve's target users are tutors teaching local Singapore students,
whose phone numbers are 8 digits. AB3 accepts any run of 3 or more
digits.

Require exactly 8 digits after removing whitespace, hyphens and
parentheses, so commonly formatted input such as "9123 4567" or
"(9123)-4567" is accepted and stored as "91234567". Keep all other
characters, including '+', so that a number with a country code such
as "+65 811878" is rejected instead of shrinking into a valid-looking
8-digit number.

Strip in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a data file with a
hand-edited, formatted phone still loads instead of being discarded.
The Phone constructor stays strict and accepts only 8 digits.

Update test fixtures to use 8-digit phones, and add tests for
stripping, rejected input and loading formatted phones from JSON.

Addresses accept any length, so a very long address stretches the
client card in the UI. Repeated whitespace typed or pasted into an
address is also stored as is.

Trim the ends and collapse consecutive whitespace into a single space,
then reject addresses longer than 150 characters. Check the length
after collapsing, so stray spaces do not count against the limit.

Normalize in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a hand-edited
address with extra whitespace or a line break in the data file still
loads.

Names accept only alphanumeric characters and spaces, so real names
such as "O'Brien", "Nur-Aisyah" or "David Ray Jr." are rejected,
while input starting with a digit or symbol is accepted.

Require names to start with a letter, followed by letters, digits,
spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops, up to 50 characters.
Keep '/' disallowed, as it is the prefix delimiter, so a name such
as "a/l" cannot be misread as an address.

Trim the ends and collapse consecutive whitespace before validating,
in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a hand-edited name with
extra spaces in the data file still loads.

commitResults.messageBody:

"John Doe" and "owesMoney".

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix singular and plural counts in messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The find result reads "1 clients found", and the out-of-range index
error has three versions: delete says "1 items", tag says "1 item(s)"
and edit says "The client index provided is invalid".

Share one out-of-range message across delete, tag and edit and

and "clients". Check the literal message text for counts of 0, 1 and
2, so the tests catch wording errors that comparing against the
constant would hide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect duplicate clients regardless of name case
commitResults.messageBody:
Duplicate detection compares names exactly, so "john tan" and
"John Tan" are added as two different clients. The duplicate message
also does not say which client is clashing or what to do next.

Treat clients with the same name, ignoring case, as duplicates in add,
edit and the data file. Rename Person.isSamePerson to hasSameName
to reflect this. Use the new Person.hasSamePhone to tell the two
cases apart: when the phone also matches, report that the client
already exists; otherwise, ask the user to check the details and
suggest adding an identifier such as "John Neo (NHHS)". Allow
parentheses in names so that this suggestion is a valid name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an undo history to the model
commitResults.messageBody:

to, but the model only holds the current state.

Add VersionedAddressBook, which saves a copy of the client list after
each change, and expose commitAddressBook, canUndoAddressBook and
undoAddressBook through Model. Nothing calls commitAddressBook yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save the client list to the undo history after each command
commitResults.messageBody:
The undo history only grows when something calls commitAddressBook.

Let's make LogicManager call commitAddressBook after every command that runs
successfully. To keep list, find and other commands that change
nothing out of the history, commitAddressBook now does nothing when
the client list is the same as the last saved state.

Tutors can type a valid command that does the wrong thing, such as
deleting the wrong client or clearing the list by accident, and have
no way to reverse it.

Add an undo command that reverts the last change to the client list,
using the undo history saved after each command. Undo shows the full
list afterwards, so that a restored client is not hidden by an earlier
find. It is blocked in read-only mode like other commands that change
data and is listed in the help window.

The user guide has no section for undo, and the developer guide still
describes AB3's proposed undo/redo design, which differs from what
Sieve implements.

Add an undo section and command summary row to the user guide.
Replace the developer guide's proposed design with the actual one: a
stack of earlier client lists, saved by LogicManager after each
successful command and skipped when nothing changed. Redraw the undo
diagrams to match and add manual test cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add CommandHistory to track entered commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Users must retype a whole command to fix a typo or repeat it, which is
slow for long commands such as edit.

Let's add a CommandHistory class that stores every command entered in
the session and lets callers step back and forward through them.

CommandHistory has no JavaFX code, so its behaviour can be checked
with plain unit tests before it is connected to the command box.

The tests cover stepping back and forward, both ends of the history,
repeated commands and adding a command after going back.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recall previous commands with Up and Down keys
commitResults.messageBody:
Users must retype a whole command to repeat it or fix a typo, which is
slow for long commands such as edit.

Let's connect CommandHistory to CommandBox:
* add every entered command to the history, even if it fails, so a
  mistyped command can be brought back and fixed
* show the previous or next command when Up or Down is pressed with
  the cursor at the end

Other keys are left to the text field, so the cursor can still be moved
within a recalled command.

Users and developers have no way to learn that Up and Down recall
earlier commands.

Let's,
* add a UG section on recalling commands with Up and Down
* add a DG section with a sequence diagram and design considerations
* add CommandHistory to the UI class diagram
* add manual tests for recalling commands

CommandBox had no tests, so the Up and Down handling added for the
command history was not covered.

Let's test CommandBox with TestFX, as HelpWindowTest does, using a stub

are fired directly, so the tests do not depend on window focus.

commitResults.messageTitle: Count case-only edits to tags as changes that can be undone
commitResults.messageBody:
Person#equals compares tags with Tag#equals, which ignores case so
that a client cannot have both Math and math. As a result, a client
tagged Math equals the same client tagged MATH. An edit that only
changes a tag's case is saved to the data file, but
VersionedAddressBook#commitAddressBook() sees no change and skips the
commit. The next undo then reverts it together with the change before
it, and redo cannot bring it back.

Let's compare tag names exactly in Person#equals. Tag#equals is
unchanged, so adding of duplicate tags are still detected ignoring
case.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a neutral icon when a search finds no clients
commitResults.messageBody:
When find or filter matches no clients, the result line shows the
green success tick. The command did run correctly, but nothing was
found, so the tick suggests a result that is not there.

Let's add an emptySearch flag to CommandResult, set by find and filter
when nothing matches, and have ResultDisplay show a grey "i" through
an :empty-search pseudo-class instead of the tick.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the full email and the phone on every client card
commitResults.messageBody:
The email label on the client card cannot be narrower than its full
text. A very long email makes the card wider than the list, which
pushes the phone number out of view, even at 800px wide. Shortening
the email with an ellipsis instead would hide part of it, and labels
cannot be copied, so the tutor could not read it anywhere.

Let's put the email and the address on their own lines and let them
wrap, so both are always shown in full and the card always fits the
list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let long command results scroll instead of being cut off
commitResults.messageBody:
Deleting many clients gives a result too long for the result line.
It was cut off after about 9 clients with no way to see the rest, and
it squeezed the client list.

Put the result in a WrappingScrollPane capped at 7 lines, so a longer
result scrolls and the client list keeps the rest of the window.
Page Up and Page Down in the command box scroll the result, so it can
be read without leaving the keyboard.

Update the UG and DG to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unknown prefixes in add and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The tokenizer only splits off the prefixes a command knows, so an
unknown one, such as a mistyped z/, stays inside the value before it.
add n/Amy ... a/Blk 1 z/x saves the address as "Blk 1 z/x" without
any warning.

Let's reject a word that looks like a prefix in any value except the
note, where text such as w/ (with) is normal.

The UG never says which characters a name may contain, so users only
find out from the error message, and nothing says that names with
s/o or accented letters are not supported.

Let's list the name rules under add, with a workaround for those
names, and link to them from edit.
Add read-only activity diagram to DG

Any 8 digits are accepted as a phone number, including 00000000 and
12345678, and an email domain does not need a dot, so a@bc and
a@localhost are accepted. None of these can be a real client's
contact.

Let's accept only Singapore numbers, which start with 3, 6, 8 or 9,
and require a dot in the email domain.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain asserts and fix inaccurate comments
commitResults.messageBody:
The asserts in VersionedAddressBook and Command#getDuplicateMessage
say what must hold but not why it can never fail. A reader cannot
tell whether a failure means bad input or a bug.

Some comments also no longer match the code:
* PREFIX_LIKE_WORD says such a word comes after a space but it is
  also matched at the start of a value, as in a/z/x.
* CommandHistory says only non-empty commands are kept but the blank
  check is in CommandBox. Its index comment is also wrong when no
  command has been recalled.
* Undo and redo show the full list so a restored client is not hidden
  by a find but filter narrows the list too.
* TagColor names only LightTheme.css, but DarkTheme.css also has a
  rule for each color.
* Several comments use British spelling, against the coding standard.

Let's add a comment to each assert saying why it holds, and correct
those comments.

# Conflicts:
#	src/test/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindowTest.java
#	src/test/java/seedu/address/ui/ResultDisplayTest.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain country codes and limit email length
commitResults.messageBody:
A phone number with a country code, such as +65 9123 4567, gets the
general phone error, which doesn't say that Sieve leaves the country
code out. An email has no length limit, and one that is thousands of
characters long overflows the stack of the email regex, so the command
silently does nothing. The email error also does not say which rule
was broken.

Let's give a specific error for a number with a country code, and
explain in the UG why Sieve leaves it out. Let's also accept emails of
up to 254 characters, checked before the regex, and list the email
rules in the error message and in the UG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make undo, redo, clear and edit less surprising
commitResults.messageBody:
undo 3 and redo 2 undo or redo a single change without saying so and
clear 3 deletes every client instead of client 3.

An edit that changes nothing reports "Edited client" but adds nothing
to the undo history, so the next undo reverts an older change that the
user did not expect. edit and add also reset a filtered list to all
clients without saying so.

Let's
* make clear, undo and redo reject any parameters,
* report "No change" when an edit leaves the client as it was, and
  keep the displayed list,
* end the add and edit results with "Showing all clients.".

commitResults.messageTitle: Report unknown prefixes and bad indices precisely
commitResults.messageBody:
A mistyped required prefix, such as P/ for p/, or an unknown prefix
before the first real one, such as edit 1 z/x n/Amy, shows the
generic "Invalid command format!" instead of naming the prefix.
edit 0 shows the whole usage instead of the index error, and an index
too large for an int is called "not a positive integer". An address
made only of a non-breaking space is accepted and shows as blank.

Let's
* check add and edit for unknown prefixes, including in the
  preamble, before the other format checks,
* show the index error for an invalid edit index, as delete does,
* treat an index too large for an int as out of bounds,
* require an address to contain a letter or digit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long names and tidy the UI code
commitResults.messageBody:
At the minimum window width, a long name is cut off with "...", which
hides the "(NHHS)" suffix that the UG suggests adding. The command box
placeholder is also cut off, at "or type he".

The UI code has some loose ends too:
* PersonCard repeats setVisible and setManaged for five parts of the
  card, and ResultDisplay does the same twice.
* ResultDisplay#showMessage clears the empty-search style, and then
  its caller sets it again.
* The CommandResult field emptySearch does not sound like a boolean.
* WrappingScrollPane does not say that it relies on fitToWidth.
* LightTheme.css has rules that never apply, and hard-coded colors
  that make DarkTheme.css copy a whole rule. It also has 5-space
  indents, British spelling, and comments about a mockup that readers
  do not have.

Let's wrap the name, shorten the placeholder, add a setShown helper
to UiPart, and clean up the rest without changing how the app looks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep half-typed command and ignore Shift+Up
commitResults.messageBody:
Pressing Up while typing a command replaces the half-typed text with
the previous command. Pressing Down past the newest command only
clears the box, so the half-typed command is lost for good.

Shift+Up, Cmd+Up and similar keys also recall commands, instead of
selecting text or moving the cursor as they do in other text boxes.

The code around them has some loose ends too:
* CommandBox#handleKeyPressed calls event.consume() in three places.
* The CommandBox constructor does not check its arguments for null.
* CommandHistory calls its index "current", and increments it in two
  branches.

Let's keep the text in the box when the user first presses Up, and
show it again after the newest command, as bash does. Let's also
leave Up and Down with a modifier key to the text field, and tidy
both classes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve test case design and remove duplication
commitResults.messageBody:
Several of my tests repeat the same setup, e.g. deleting Alice and
committing appears 11 times in VersionedAddressBookTest. Some input
partitions are never tested: the unknown-prefix check has no unit
test, CommandBox never sees a ParseException, and nothing checks that
both themes style every tag color. One email case breaks two rules at
once, so it pins neither. ResultDisplayTest also depends on the window
size left by an earlier test, and fails when the test order changes.

Let's move the repeated setup into helpers, add a test for each
missing partition and boundary, keep to one invalid input per case,
and size the window to the scene in every layout test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy up code, input errors and card layout
commitResults.messageBody:
Some code is repeated or inconsistent. Name, Address and Note each
normalize whitespace with the same code, add and edit each list the
same prefixes by hand, and "Showing all clients." is typed in four
messages, after a space in undo and redo but on a new line in add and
edit. getDuplicateMessage sits in Command, although only add and edit
use it.

Some input errors are also less helpful than they could be. add does
not say which compulsory prefix is missing, p/0065 9123 4567 gets the
generic phone error instead of the country-code one, and the address
error does not say what to enter for a client without an address.

On a client card, the phone number is centered beside the name, so
when a long name wraps, it sits lower than the name's first line.

Let's
* move the shared code into StringUtil, CliSyntax and Messages,
* name the missing prefixes in add's error,
* treat 0065 followed by 8 digits as a country code,
* suggest a/Online in the address error,
* align the phone number with the name's baseline, and
* tidy a few names, comments and the color spelling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fill test gaps and trim duplicated tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Some cases in my code have no test: which of a client's fee, due date
and note the card shows, editing a recalled command, a tag edit that
only changes case, the preamble check for unknown prefixes, the
"Showing all clients." text, and some address and country code
boundaries. Other tests repeat each other: a third no-change edit
test, near copies of the long name and long email card checks,
whitespace cases that StringUtilTest now owns, and country code
cases that PhoneTest owns.

Let's add a test for each missing case, keep each partition in one
test class, and share the repeated card, key and result display
checks through helpers.
Fill test gaps and trim duplicated tests

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix help order and empty-list placeholder tip
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window listed undo after untag, out of alphabetical order
(#187). Also, with no clients at all, the list's placeholder said
"Use list to show all clients", which can't help, as every client
is already shown (#189).

Let's move undo above untag, and let the placeholder suggest only
add when Sieve has no clients, and list when a search or filter
hides them. Logic#getAllPersonList exposes the unfiltered list so
PersonListPanel can tell the two cases apart.

Fixes #187, fixes #189.
Treat tags that differ only in spaces as equal
Show tips when filter finds no clients
Accept data files saved with a byte order mark

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix user guide examples, links and gaps
commitResults.messageBody:
Testers read the user guide first, and several parts of it no longer
match the app. A delete example fails on the sample data, the site
nav's Command Summary link opens the FAQ, the quoted delete error and
the help section are out of date, and a known issue describes a bug
that is fixed. Some limits are not stated, such as names with @ or a
comma, addresses, and undo not saying which change it reverted. The
README badges are broken, and SettingUp.md still asks for JDK 17.

Let's correct these, state the limits as not supported, and delete
Configuration.md and the unused AB3 diagrams and images.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bring the developer guide in line with the code
commitResults.messageBody:
Parts of the developer guide no longer match the code. The Model
diagram has no VersionedAddressBook, the UI section ignores the dark
theme's stylesheet, and the delete sequence diagram creates the
command before parsing its indexes. Undo and input validation have no
use case or implementation section, use case UC3A lacks its endings,
and the glossary calls tags alphanumeric. Nothing explains why the
code says Person and AddressBook where the guide says client.

Let's fix the diagrams and text, add the missing use case, section,
user stories and manual tests, and explain the AB3 class names.
Fix abstraction level, remove name predicate
Improve defensive code and logging in find
Fix missing fee and due date
Fix data file location in the UG
Require the note to be the last parameter
Add manual tests for add, edit, notes and names
Add a detailed client interface
Branch fix bugs in untag tags

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix detail panel regressions and tidy up for v1.5
commitResults.messageBody:
The new client detail panel breaks a few things:

* Clicking a client card or the panel's X button takes the keyboard
  focus from the command box, so typing and the Up and Down keys no
  longer reach it.
* After undo, find, filter or an edit in a filtered list, the panel
  shows whichever client is now in the same row. Deleting the shown
  client moves the panel to the next client.
* At the 450 px minimum window width, the open panel runs past the
  window's edge and hides its X button.
* In the narrow list beside the panel, a name can run into the phone
  number, e.g. "Devi Ramasamy81234567".

Also, clear says "All client data has been cleared." even when there
are no clients.

Let's
* stop the client list and the X button from taking the focus,
* reselect the same client by name after the list changes, or the
  client that replaced it after a rename, and close the panel if it
  is no longer shown,
* raise the minimum window width to 600 px,
* add a gap between the name and the phone number, and
* say that there are no clients to clear, without changing anything.

While we are here, let's also
* use the theme's border color for the X button,
* share the sorted tag labels between PersonCard and
  PersonDetailPanel,
* reuse StringUtil#normalizeWhitespace in Tag#normalizeTagName,
* append to ArgumentMultimap's value lists instead of copying them,
* fix two Javadoc comments, and
* bump the version to v1.5.

Fixes #157.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update docs for the note rule and detail panel
commitResults.messageBody:
Recent merges left the docs behind the code. The DG's input validation
section says notes may contain any prefix, though #161 now rejects a
known one. A merge dropped use case UC2's no-change extension, and
another brought back an outdated note rule in the UG's edit section.
The UG's due-date example, 01-11-2026, will be rejected as a past date
from 1 Nov, and a DG manual test still expects the old sample due date.
The FAQ has one question, and the UG doesn't say that long names now
get an error with their length.

Let's describe the note rule and how the detail panel affects the
empty list, restore the lost extension, drop the outdated line, move
the due dates to 2030, and add two FAQ entries.
Fix tag display in success message when there is no tag
